description:
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)  

  Multi-Layered Market, Technology, and Business Analysis Services  

  Issuing Agency:   

 Secretary of the Air Force, Office of Competitive Activities (SAF/OC) 

 Office of Commercial and Economic Analysis (SAF/OCXA) 

  Classification:  UNCLASSIFIED // CUI 

 1. Purpose and Authority 

 This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes by the United States Air Force on behalf of the Office of Commercial and Economic Analysis (OCEA). This announcement constitutes market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with response preparation. 

 2. Background and Strategic Context 

 Modern strategic competition requires the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and the broader Department of Defense (DoD) enterprise to maintain deep visibility into dynamic commercial markets, global supply chains, emerging technology ecosystems, and adversary geoeconomic strategies. OCEA delivers commercially grounded, data-driven, and forward-looking economic and technological intelligence to senior defense decision-makers across three core strategic lines of effort: Speed Us Up, Slow Them Down, and Move the Goal Post. 

 3. Mission Objectives and Analytical Operating Model 

 OCEA operates across five core mission areas: (1) Entity Risk Analysis, (2) Technology Analysis, (3) Trade and Supply Analysis, (4) Sector and Market Analysis, and (5) Geoeconomic Analysis. 

 4. Anticipated Scope of Services 

 4.1 Sector, Market, and Geoeconomic Analysis 

 Conduct multi-layered sector, market, and geoeconomic analysis examining business ecosystems, corporate actors, investment flows, technology maturity and diffusion, industrial capacity, trade and supply dependencies, intellectual property and patent activity, and relevant geopolitical or regulatory conditions. Monitor and assess global private-equity, venture-capital, and cross-border investment flows, translating market developments into actionable risk assessments. 

 4.2 Entity Risk and Corporate Due Diligence 

 Perform commercial Due Diligence, Research Security reviews, and entity risk analysis on commercial vendors, research institutes, covered individuals, and corporate networks in accordance with: 

 
	 Public Law 117-183 (SBIR and STTR Extension Act of 2022), 
	 Public Law 119-83 (Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act / 15 U.S.C. § 638(vv)), 
	 AFI 61-102_DAFGM 2026-01, 
	 FY25 NDAA Section 911 (10 U.S.C. § 9035), 
	 May 2024 DEPSECDEF Memorandum (Defense SBIR/STTR Due Diligence Program), 
	 NSPM-33 
	 DoW SCRM Risk Taxonomy 2.1, and 
	 DoD Instruction 2000.25 (CFIUS). 
 

 4.3 Technology Analysis 

 Analyze technology maturity, diffusion rates, technical dependencies, manufacturing feasibility, patent and IP trends, critical inputs, and dual-use applications across priority defense sectors. Assess how private capital, public investments, export controls, and supply-chain constraints affect technology scale-up, production resilience, and allied access. 

 4.4 Trade and Supply Analysis 

 Provide continuous trade and supply analysis, including automated Tier-N supply-chain illumination, value-chain mapping, and continuous monitoring of raw-material constraints, manufacturing dependencies, logistics bottlenecks, and critical single-point failures. Use predictive modeling to project impacts of geopolitical events, sanctions, export restrictions, and market shifts. 

 4.5 Analytical Production and Two-Tier Quality Control 

 Produce decision-ready written deliverables, executive summaries, risk matrices, and briefings tailored to Government timelines. Deliverables include multi-agent AI-generated Deep Dive Reports (DDRs) (~10–20 pages), Open-Source Reports (OSRs), and rapid risk assessments. Maintain a standard baseline production capacity of ~24 DDRs/week (~1,200 DDRs annually) scaling to surge capacities of 32+ DDRs/week or more. 

 4.6 Workflow, Data, Automation, and Tool Integration 

 Operate within Department-approved secure workflows and enterprise tools baselined within the Department of the Air Force (DAF) Impact Level 5 (IL5) Generative AI secure cloud workspace. Commercial cloud environments may be leveraged when capabilities exceed government cloud environments and higher security environments are not required for official production deliverables. The contractor must fully integrate operations within the DAF Microsoft 365 enterprise suite (Forms intake, Planner RFI Backlog, SharePoint repository, and Power Automate orchestration) and Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environment. Execute automated batch intake for high-volume defense proposal transfers. Support technical solutions engineering: process mapping, automation runbooks, standard operating procedure (SOP) maintenance, API integrations, and interactive dashboards within DAF Microsoft 365 Suite and AFRL GCP providing unified pipeline visibility across Due Diligence, Research Security, and SCRM workflows. 

 4.7 Advisory, Portfolio, and Stakeholder Support 

 Provide flexible analytical and advisory teams to support portfolio-level risk management, ad-hoc inquiry bursts, and interagency stakeholder engagements across 30+ USG partner. Prepare presentation packages and facilitate Risk Review Boards (RRBs) for AFWERX Small Business Concern (SBC) applicants and AFOSR fundamental research grant proposals in compliance with AFI 61-102_DAFGM 2026-01 and NSPM-33. Deliver structured training modules (e.g., DD 001 Intro to Due Diligence, DD 101 Data Interpretation) and support tabletop exercises. 

 4.8 DoW & DAF Foreign Risk Evaluation
